cards.text: The scribes and chief priests know Jesus just told a parable against them, and they want Him arrested. But they're afraid of the people. So they watch Him closely and send spies who pretend to be sincere.

cards.question: The spies are only pretending to be sincere. What are they really hoping to do?
If the spies can catch Jesus, the plan is to hand Him over to the rule and authority of the ___.

cards.text: The spies walk up all smiles: “Teacher,” they say, “we know that You speak and teach correctly.” Friend, that's the coworker who tells you you're AMAZING at spreadsheets right before he hands you his.

cards.question: After all that flattery, what question do the spies ask Jesus?

answers.text: Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar
Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath
Is it lawful to divorce a wife

cards.question: Jesus falls for the spies' act.

cards.text: Jesus sees right through them and says, “Show Me a denarius.” That's the moment the guy setting the trap looks down and realizes he's the one standing in it.

cards.question: Jesus asks whose image and inscription are on the denarius. The spies answer that they belong to ___.
Caesar's face is on the coin the spies are holding. So what does Jesus tell them?

answers.text: Give Caesar what is his and God what is His
Pay Caesar nothing and give it all to God
Pay Caesar first and give God what is left

cards.text: The people are watching. The spies spent all that time building this trap, and now they wait to see if it snaps shut.

cards.question: The spies manage to trap Jesus in His words in front of the people.
The spies are ___ at Jesus' answer, and they fall ___.

cards.text: Round two. Some Sadducees, a group of Jewish leaders, come to question Jesus.

cards.question: The Sadducees say there is no resurrection.

cards.text: They open with something Moses wrote, about a man whose brother dies and leaves a wife but no children.

cards.question: According to what Moses wrote, what is the living brother supposed to do?

answers.text: Marry the widow and raise children for his brother
Look after the widow until she marries again
Give the widow his brother's land and house

cards.text: Now their story: there were seven brothers. SEVEN. The first one married a wife but died childless.

cards.question: Then the second brother and the third marry the widow. How does it go for all seven brothers?

answers.text: All seven die and leave no children
The seventh brother finally has a son
The last brother refuses to marry her

cards.text: And last of all, the woman dies. Friend, I've heard shorter setups from a man asking to borrow twenty dollars.

cards.question: Here's the Sadducees' big question: in the resurrection, whose ___ will she be?

cards.text: Jesus answers, “The sons of this age marry and are given in marriage.” Notice that word, friend. THIS age.

cards.question: Jesus says those worthy to share in the age to come and in the resurrection will still marry.
Jesus says those in the resurrection can no longer die. Why?

answers.text: Because they are like the angels
Because they never sinned on earth
Because they ate from the tree of life

cards.text: Since they are sons of the resurrection, Jesus says, they are sons of God. Then He says even Moses, the same Moses the Sadducees just quoted, shows that the dead are raised.

cards.question: To show it, Jesus points to the passage about the burning ___.

cards.text: There Moses calls the Lord “the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.” Those three, Israel's forefathers, had all died long before Moses (Genesis 25:8; 35:29; 49:33).

cards.question: Jesus says the Lord is not the God of the ___, but of the ___, for to Him all are alive.

cards.text: Some of the scribes answer, “Teacher, You have spoken well!” The SCRIBES, friend, and I'd sit down from shock if I could ever get off this gold base.

cards.question: After all that, what do the people questioning Jesus do?

answers.text: They don't dare question Him any further
They bring Him an even harder question
They ask Him to show them a sign

findings.problem: The joke says the trap-setter realizes he's the one standing in his own trap. That tells the baker the spies' trap fails, which gives away card 11 (the spies don't trap Jesus in His words, Luke 20:26). It also says the spies 'realize' something the text hasn't shown yet at verse 24.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: 'The spies spent all that time building this trap' adds a detail the text doesn't give. Luke 20:20 says only that they watched Him closely and sent spies. Also, 'now they wait to see if it snaps shut' is a flat line with almost none of Papa Dorin's voice.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can add a storyteller's line to carry the moment, like "But the Lord isn't finished with him," as long as it adds no facts.

findings.problem: The right answer is the only one in the famous biblical 'Give ... what is his' phrasing. Both wrong answers start with a modern-sounding 'Pay Caesar...', so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The card cites Luke 20:30-31, but the right answer (all seven die and leave no children) is only in Luke 20:31. Verse 30 belongs to the setup in the question, not the answer.

rule.text: A choice card cites only the verses of its right answer.

findings.problem: The joke 'I'd sit down from shock if I could ever get off this gold base' doesn't click right away. Not being able to sit down has no clear link to standing on a base, so the line needs explaining. The sentence 'The SCRIBES, friend, and I'd sit down...' is also awkward.

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining.

findings.problem: This story card is a bare summary with no Papa Dorin voice.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: This story card reads like a reference note, with a quote and then a list of Genesis citations, and has no Papa Dorin voice.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The walkthrough has only about four real jokes (stop 1 cards 4 and 7, stop 2 cards 7 and 16). Many story cards read pleasant but flat: stop 1 card 1, stop 2 cards 1, 5, 12 and 14. Several moments could hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, like the seven-brothers setup or the Sadducees quoting Moses and then hearing Moses quoted back.

rule.text: When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
